answer.sce667889: Add Quark and turn on member logs. Each time someone joins, Quark posts a log with the invite link they used and the member who created it.
answer.sd2556319: Quark logs images and files posted in your server, including ones that are later deleted, so moderators can review them. It is not an IP grabber. Discord does not share IP addresses or locations with bots, so Quark cannot collect them.
answer.sd4808d78: The audit log is Discord's built-in list of administrative actions, kept in Server Settings for 45 days. A mod log is a channel in your own server where a bot posts each action as a message, so it lasts, can be read by anyone you allow, and can include things the audit log leaves out, like deleted message content.
answer.sd4c6d2f8: Logs are a running record of what happens in a server: messages deleted or edited, members joining and leaving, voice activity, and moderation actions. Moderators use them to check what happened after the fact.
answer.sd65a2956: Yes. Quark only handles logging, so it does not clash with Dyno's moderation, automod or custom commands. Run both, and turn off Dyno's Action Log module so each event is only logged once.
answer.sd734498e: Quark automations are rules that watch the logs Quark already makes for a Discord server and act when one matches. A rule reads as one sentence: when a log is produced, and only if some conditions are true, then do something. It can alert a channel and ping a role, add a notice to the log, copy the log to another channel or hold it back.
answer.sda384a77: Anyone who can see the log channel you pick. Most servers make that channel visible to staff only. Quark posts nothing in public channels unless you point it at one.
answer.sda8ccbb5: Quark is a Discord bot built only for logging, and it runs alongside MEE6. MEE6's help centre says its audit logs all go to one channel and are posted in bulk every 1 to 5 minutes. Quark logs events as they happen, sends each category of log to its own channel, and keeps deleted images and files as well as the text of deleted messages.
answer.se04c4a29: Yes. When a message with an image or file is deleted, the log includes the attachment, so you can still open it after it has been removed from the channel.
answer.se59d65e1: No. Quark does not do reaction roles, word filters, custom commands or starboards. It has /ban, /kick, /mute and /purge, tags, and rules that act on your logs. If you use Carl-bot for the rest, keep it and let Quark take over the logging.
answer.se641efe7: To set up logs on a Discord server, create a private text channel for your staff, invite a logging bot such as Quark, and run /logging to choose that channel. Logging starts straight away and the whole setup takes about two minutes. A bot is needed because Discord's own audit log only records administrative actions, and only keeps them for 45 days.
answer.se844f101: No. Those plugins modify the Discord app on your own device, which Discord's terms of service do not allow. Quark is a bot that a server's staff add to their own server, and it only logs what happens in that server.
answer.seaa5b8bc: Yes. The free plan includes every log type, a channel for each category of log, ignore rules and the live web viewer, and it keeps the content of deleted messages that are up to 12 hours old. Quark Pro extends that to 4 weeks and adds 30 days of searchable log history on the web, CSV export, and the moderator behind server mutes and deafens.
answer.seb18cf58: Quark is a Discord bot built only for logging, and it runs alongside ProBot. ProBot's pricing page lists “Executioner in logs”, the person behind an action, and voice move and disconnect logs as premium features. Quark names the moderator and the reason on bans, kicks, timeouts and role changes on its free plan, and logs voice moves there too.
answer.seb862c24: Quark keeps a copy of the image or file and posts it with the log. Dyno's documentation says it does not log the file or embed content of a deleted message, and YAGPDB's says it records the attachment's URL. answer.see57130f: No. Logger's website says its stored data was wiped when it shut down, and no bot can recover what another bot stored. The log messages Logger posted in your channels are still there. Quark logs from the moment it joins your server.
answer.sf107ce7f: Create a private channel for your staff, invite Quark, and run /logging to choose that channel. Logging starts straight away and the whole setup takes about two minutes.
answer.sf820007a: No. Logger's website says the bot shut down in April 2024, after seven years, and that its stored data was wiped that day. Bots called Logger on bot lists today are copies run by other people.
answer.sfa45164b: On the free plan, Quark keeps the content of a message for 12 hours. A message deleted or edited within that time is logged in full; an older one is still logged, but without its text or attachments. Quark Pro keeps content for 4 weeks.
answer.sfad59db0: Yes, if you are comfortable running a server. Logger's website says its code stays on GitHub so people can host their own copy. You would need to run and update it yourself. Quark is hosted for you, so there is nothing to keep online.
